review_notes: Scope: selected the first contribution stated in the introduction—the total-AQ cost-of-capital tests—in its full specification: Table 2 Panel B / Eq. (2), Table 2 Panel C / Eq. (3), and Table 3 Panel A / Eq. (7). Eq. (1) is included as the AQ-measure construction dependency; Eq. (6) is included because the authors report Eq. (7) incremental adjusted R-squared relative to it.

The introduction also calls innate-versus-discretionary pricing a second contribution. Its later Hypothesis 2 decomposition (Section 5, Table 4), alternative AQ measures, unreported rating tests, quintile beta sort, and lower-order CAPM specifications are excluded as a distinct later decomposition, robustness/application, or preliminary/nested specification under the one-principal-family selection rule.

The paper does not name the within-fit estimator for Eq. (1), Eqs. (2)–(3), or Eqs. (6)–(7). Fama–MacBeth identifies the time-series inference for annual tests, not the underlying annual estimator. The Beta control in Eq. (3) comes from firm-specific CAPM fits described in words; the firm-level equation is not printed.

Table 2’s quintile heading says Q1 is the high AQ score and Q5 the low AQ score, while the text calls Q5 the poorest-quality group and the raw AQ measure is residual standard deviation with larger values indicating poorer quality. The numerical decile-rank direction for Eqs. (2)–(3) remains ambiguous.
results_review_notes: The selected baseline family is Table 2 Panel B, Table 2 Panel C, and Table 3 Panel A, three-factor-plus-AQfactor. Other Table 2 quintile outcomes, alternate asset-pricing columns, decomposition tables, and subsequent analyses are not added.
Table 1 summaries are retained only for selected outcomes, model variables, and upstream raw versions/components. No table values were recalculated.

Table 1 does not report direct data summaries for IntCov, Beta, monthly excess returns, SMB, HML, or AQfactor; the AQ summary is an upstream sorting input to AQfactor, not a direct AQfactor return summary.

Table 2 Panel B retains the printed coefficient cells. The AQ result discussion converts 0.14 across nine AQ decile differences to 126 basis points, indicating that Panel B coefficients are displayed in percentage-point units relative to CostDebt’s ratio scale; the coefficient multiplier records that source-supported scale.
